newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says Vietnamese refugees agree to go home.
newsitem.headline: Manila says Vietnamese refugees agree to go home.

text.p: A group of Vietnamese refugees in the Philippines have agreed to go home after the United States offered to give them cash incentives, a Philippine government official said on Friday.
"We were told (by the U.S. embassy in Manila) that 88 Vietnamese refugees have volunteered to be repatriated," the official from the Foreign Affairs Department told reporters.
The official said the 88 were among 345 Vietnamese refugees who were refused entry to the United States in the late 1980s.
They volunteered to be repatriated after the U.S. government offered a cash incentive of $1,000 for each adult refugee and $5,000 for children up to 13 years old, he said.
The refugees were given until June 30 this year to take up the cash incentive, the official added..
The Philippine official said Hanoi had agreed to speed up the processing of the papers of the refugees.
The 345 Vietnamese "political refugees" are in a refugee camp in the south western Philippine island of Palawan. There are at least 1,000 Vietnamese refugees left in the camp.
They were among 2,500 Vietnamese originally in the camp who were denied asylum in the United States and other western countries.
